### ⭐ The instrument hazard was not just avoided — its reason was measured

The dispatch warned that a DOM assertion is blind here. You went one better and **measured why**, rather than inheriting it:

> `packages/components/src/ui/sheet.tsx` and `.../ui/dialog.tsx` **BOTH import `@radix-ui/react-dialog`, and neither stamps a `data-slot`**. `drawer` and `modal` therefore reach the DOM as the same Radix role, separated only by Tailwind class strings. A DOM assertion cannot tell them apart **even on the renderer that gets this right**.

⇒ that last clause is the proof. It is not "a DOM test would be weak here"; it is "**a DOM test reads identically on the control**", which makes it no instrument at all. ⚠️ And it is why my own grep found `toBeVisible` once and had to be enumerated — the hit is the sentence explaining the trap, not an instance of it.

### ⭐ Neither number means anything without the other, and the file says so

> The LIVE CONTROL for the instrument used here is `ObjectTree.overlayShellControl-9113.test.tsx`, which reads **FOUR** distinct boundary pairs off the identical technique; this file reads **ONE**. **Neither number means anything without the other.**

⭐ That is the whole shape of a measurement round done right: the same technique, two renderers, one known-good. A "1" alone would have been consistent with a broken probe.

The control file also carries `LIT CONTROL: the shell-boundary instrument fires at all` as a separate row **before** the reading it supports — so an instrument failure reports as an instrument failure rather than as a finding.

### ⭐⭐ The round's real product is a reframing, and it is carried where it can be acted on

Question 1 is answered **by execution**: the `Sheet` is the **CONTAINER** — the payload renders in the modal, split and popover shells behind a lit drawer control. ⇒ **portability is not the blocker**, so the open question is a **product** one.

I verified the sub-premise correction myself rather than relaying it: the triage fence named record fetching among four blockers, and **`RecordDetailDrawer` does not fetch** — `record` is a required prop, `objectSchema?` optional (`RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:54-74`), no fetch inside. Three of the four travel with the payload.

I also re-verified both narrowings independently:
- **`popover` is honoured NOWHERE** — `popoverTrigger` appears only in `navigation-overlay.tsx` (declaration, destructure, the `!popoverTrigger` guard, two render sites) plus **one comment** at `ObjectView.tsx:2228` documenting the fallback. **Zero renderers pass it** ⇒ it degrades to a compact `Dialog` on **five** surfaces.
- **`ObjectTree` + authored `split` renders NOTHING** — the branch needs `mainContent`, which the tree never passes.

⇒ **filed as objectui#9299 with the `needs-user-decision` label**, carrying the measurement, the three priced routes and a PM recommendation. ⛔ Correct that you filed neither narrowing as its own card: both are **inputs to that one ruling**, not separable repairs.

### ⭐ Declining to recommend was right, and flagging the template conflict was better

> this report template presumes a recommendation field, and this card's fence forbids one. The fence wins; the field is answered with the pricing above and no choice.

⛔ A seat may not take this decision, and you did not. ⭐ Surfacing that your own report shape disagreed with the fence — instead of quietly filling the field — is what let me carry the pricing forward intact.

### One instrument fault, caught and reported
The question-1 probe's **lit control failed on its first run** (a network escape to `localhost:3000`, plus an over-loose title assertion). Read as **NOT MEASURED**, repaired with a module-scope fetch double, re-run green. ⛔ Not reported as a negative answer — on the exact question the whole card turns on.

Card objectui#9113 is now **`pm:blocked`** on objectui#9299. This PR lands the measurement; the ruling is the maintainer's.
